root_idea.summary: The root centers on three semantic orientations: filling or overflowing, mixing or intermingling, and kindling or ignition.
root_idea.development: From these orientations, Classical Arabic develops usages for filled waters and vessels, flowing or hanging things, companionship and mixed coloration, and the heating or kindling of fire.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form.
Displayed under the singular passive-participle citation form.

senses.definition: To be kindled or burned in fire.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic passive use describing people being subjected to fire; the form is passive and imperfect in its attested occurrence.

senses.definition: To fill, cause to overflow, or make water flow together into one body.
senses.usage_conditions: In the passive Quranic construction concerning the seas, this supports readings in which the seas are filled, overflow, or flow together and become one sea.

senses.definition: To kindle, set ablaze, or turn into fire.
senses.usage_conditions: In the passive Quranic construction concerning the seas, this supports readings in which they are kindled, dried up through fire, or become fire.

senses.definition: Filled or full, especially describing a sea or body of water.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic passive-participle use describing the sea; the expression is also associated with readings of overflowing or being filled to capacity.

senses.definition: Filled with fire; kindled or ablaze.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-attested interpretation of the sea expression connects the participle with kindling and fire rather than water alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a river, channel, well, or vessel with water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of water filling a container or watercourse; the torrent may be the filling agent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour water into the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed transitive construction referring to forcing or pouring liquid into someone's throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To heat an oven, kindle a fire in it, or fill it with fuel; also to tend or stir its fuel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with an oven or its fuel and with the implement used to stir the fuel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to emit a prolonged yearning cry and fill her mouth with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized animal usage associated with intense yearning for the young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make hair or similar material hang down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative usage describing the arrangement or falling of hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a collar or neck-piece on a dog, or bind the dog with one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the dog-collar called سَاجُور.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To associate or interact with someone as a friend, or mix and hold intercourse with him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form III usage derived from the imagery of mutual yearning and association.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become full, especially of a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive usage describing a vessel reaching fullness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of hair, to hang down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive usage describing hair falling or extending downward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to proceed in an uninterrupted series, or to advance and hasten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of continuous, energetic movement in a line or succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Turbidness or dinginess; in the eye, a reddish or otherwise mixed discoloration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The eye usage covers an intermixture of redness or a dingy tinge in the white or dark part of the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rainwater collected in and filling a natural depression; also a rain-filled depression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is سُجَرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Full, of a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression بِئْرٌ سُجُرٌّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fuel used to heat an oven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the fuel or wood by which a tannūr is heated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A friend, close companion, or sincere associate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is سُجَرَاءُ; the meaning is figuratively connected with mutual yearning and affection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, expressly figurative or assumed-tropical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A torrent that fills everything, or a place reached and filled by a torrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The second use is a possessive or passive-like epithet for the place overrun by floodwater.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden neck-piece, or an iron collar or ring, put on a dog's neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural forms include سَوَاجِيرُ and سَوَاجِرُ; the word may denote either the material or the collar itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Turbid, muddy, or reddish, of a pool, rainwater, or drop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description includes water with mud or redness that has not yet cleared.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the white of the eye intermixed with redness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form سَجْرَاءُ is used with an eye or similar feminine noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden stick used to stir or tend fuel in an oven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A related instrumental form is مِسْجَرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Full or well-filled, of an eye, spring, or source.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical use distinct from the Quranic sea expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Containing more water than milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of milk diluted so that the water predominates over the milk itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made to flow forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participle use describing something caused to flow or pour out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Empty or drained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare contrary meaning, explicitly reported alongside the sense of being filled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Still or quiet; in some usage, still and full at the same time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use whose combination of stillness and fullness is retained where stated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of pearls, strung and hanging down, or fallen and scattered from their string.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is applied to pearls in relation to their string or their dispersal from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Highly brilliant, of a pearl.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a single pearl as a specialized descriptive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hanging down, of hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participle description of hair arranged or falling downward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a dog-collar or neck-piece attached.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a dog bearing a سَاجُور.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dried up, of water that has sunk into the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive-participle usage describing water no longer remaining on the surface.

cautions: The Quranic sea expressions support distinct traditional readings of filling or overflowing and kindling or becoming fire; these are retained as separate senses rather than collapsed into the contextual gloss alone.
Lane's printed Quran citation conventions are historical and are not used here to construct additional modern verse locations.
